title: ServerName and MailboxName expose private repr via #[non_exhaustive] but no field access
description:
pkix_identity::ServerName and pkix_identity::MailboxName are both #[non_exhaustive] pub structs with private internal repr fields. This is good from an immutability standpoint — callers construct via the parse methods and cannot access internals.

However, neither type exposes any accessor methods for the parsed content. ServerName has no way for a caller to retrieve the normalized DNS name or IP bytes. MailboxName has no way for a caller to retrieve the parsed local-part, domain, or internationalized flag. The types are opaque boxes that can only be passed to verify_dns_name/verify_mailbox.

This limits the types' utility as general-purpose parsed-identity types. Callers who want to do anything with the parsed identity (display it, log it, compare it to something other than a SAN) must re-parse the original input.

What goes wrong if this stays as-is: Callers cannot extract the normalized form of the identity after parsing. The types are parse-only, verify-only. This is a minor usability gap — the types serve their primary purpose (feeding into verify_*) correctly. But it forces callers who want the normalized DNS name (e.g. for logging or display) to normalize it themselves.

Locations:
- /home/mark/PROJECT/PKIX/pkix-identity/src/lib.rs lines 129-133 (ServerName struct, repr is private)
- /home/mark/PROJECT/PKIX/pkix-identity/src/lib.rs lines 221-236 (MailboxName struct, all fields are private)
